title: Accounts Note on a Customer Running Several Commissions
content:
# Accounts Note on a Customer Running Several Commissions

Each commission under Belrose Design Studio Custom Commissions carries its own quote, its own schedule of staged payments and its own balance, and money paid on one is never moved to another. Where a customer running several commissions asks for them to be delivered together, each is settled in full on its own terms first. An upgrade credit put toward a commission is applied to the commission it was presented against and is never spread across the customer's other commissions.

## Clauses in force

1. One quote, one staged schedule and one balance per commission; money paid on one commission is never moved to another.
2. Delivery together does not merge settlement: each commission is settled in full on its own terms first.
3. An upgrade credit is applied to the commission it was presented against, and is never spread across the customer's other commissions.

## Clauses no longer in force

Two sentences of the earlier wording of this note have been superseded by the current basis and are **no longer in force**:

> "What the customer has paid to date on a commission is read as the sum of the deposits and staged payments booked to that commission" — no longer in force.

> "it is this figure, not the quoted total, that any forfeit is taken against" — no longer in force.

Neither retired sentence is applied by the desk.

## Questions the note answers

**A customer has overpaid on one commission and owes on another. Is the surplus moved across?** No. Money paid on one commission is never moved to another.

**Two commissions are to be delivered at one appointment and one still carries a balance. Are both handed over together?** Each is settled in full on its own terms first.

**An upgrade credit was presented against one commission. May part of it be put toward a second?** No. The credit is applied to the commission it was presented against.
